verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling very dizzy with the room spinning: "I'm feeling very sick. It's probably because i'm feeling dizzy, um the the room is sort of spinning" – consistent with acute dizziness/vertigo.

Onset/time and context: "Started probably about two hours ago maybe" and "I was just actually making my husband some breakfast... I just suddenly felt very fuzzy and dizzy, um, and a bit shaky." Constant spinning: "Yeah it's, it's there, the whole time" and "the room is sort of spinning."
Unsteady gait: "I can't, I can't walk properly. Uh, well I can walk properly but not straight" and doctor: "you also mentioned that you can walk, but you're not walking straight."

Ear buzzing and no loss/pain/discharge: "my ears are buzzing a bit"; "Any kind of ear pain or ear discharge, anything like that?" – "No, nothing." Hearing: "do you have any problems hearing at the moment?..." – "No. It's just a bit of a buzzy noise in my ears, but otherwise I can hear everything."
Nausea without vomiting: "Have you been physically sick?" – "No, but now I'm feeling very sick." Doctor: "Nausea, OK." No vomiting is implied by denial of being physically sick.

No recent URI or fever: "Did you have any kind of viral illness in the recent past..." – "No." Doctor: "No cold, cough, nothing." – "No, I've been pretty healthy"; temperature: "Do you have a temperature at all?" – "I don't think so."
No limb weakness: "My, my legs and arms and everything are working fine" and doctor: "So there's no weakness of your arms and legs. OK." – "No."
Prior brief similar episode: "I had a a similar sort of thing about a month ago" and duration: "Probably only about five, ten minutes" and it "settled quite quickly."
Past medical history: "I've had premature ovarian failure".
Medication: "I've had premature ovarian failure, um, and I've taken HRT."
Allergies: "do you have any allergies at all?" – "No." This supports no known drug allergies.

Diagnosis and features: Doctor says "the most common... diagnosis we would you're suffering from at the moment is something called labyrinthitis"; continuous vertigo for ~2 hours and tinnitus and gait unsteadiness are all described earlier: onset 2 hours, "It's there, the whole time", "ear's buzzing", and difficulty walking straight.

Association of nausea with vertigo: patient links them in time – symptoms started together and says "I'm feeling very sick. It's probably because i'm feeling dizzy"; doctor labels this as "Nausea, OK."
Chronic condition and HRT: "I've had premature ovarian failure, um, and I've taken HRT." This indicates an existing (chronic) diagnosis and HRT use.

Prescription details: "I'll send the a prescription... looks like it's the Lloyd pharmacy on our system. Is that correct?" – "Yeah." and "It's called , yeah? It's one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about ten days worth." This is for symptomatic treatment of labyrinthitis/vertigo as discussed immediately prior.

In-person assessment: "I would still like you to be seen by one of our doctors to take a look inside your ears" and "while you're with the doctors, we'd like to do your blood pressure, just examine your, you know, you know, how your walking and everything is" and "In the interim, obviously in the next few days, you'll get to see one of my doctors."

Safety-netting: "if you double up any weakness of your legs or arms or, or, you know, a sudden headache. Any of those symptoms, or you start being violently sick with it, then you know, you would need to take your to A and E." This matches advice re new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, and violent vomiting.

With or without food: "can you take, do you need to take those tablets with food?" – doctor: "It doesn't really matter, you can take it, because sometimes, you know, you get the symptoms as soon as you wake up... might as well just take the tablets."

Follow-up and booking: "In the interim, obviously in the next few days, you'll get to see one of my doctors and we'll have to just take it from there" and "Just make sure you call support to book that appointment, OK?"
